chunks: And ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a tooth and an arm that are broken intentionally: is there indemnity payment for them or retaliation? He said: “Retaliation.”
He said: I said, “Then if they offer him the diyah in increased amount?” He said: “If they satisfy him with whatever he wishes, then it is his.”

key_terms.أَرْشٌ: financial indemnity or assessed compensation for an injury
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood money or financial compensation paid for bodily injury
key_terms.الذِّرَاعِ: the arm or forearm, mentioned here in the ruling on bodily injury
key_terms.السِّنِّ: a tooth, mentioned here as an injured body part subject to legal compensation or retaliation
key_terms.قَوَدٌ: retaliation (qisas), meaning equivalent legal retribution for intentional bodily harm

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for intentionally breaking a tooth or arm in Shia hadith: qisas or diyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on intentionally breaking a tooth or an arm, stating that the basic ruling is qisas (retaliation). It also indicates that if the injured party agrees to accept financial compensation instead, in whatever amount satisfies him, that settlement is valid.
